brief: Identify the policyholder, insured event and beneficiary in a fictional policy.

title.es-MX: Lee quién y qué está cubierto
title.pt-BR: Leia quem e o que está coberto

en-US.scenario: Fictional US-dollar examples for "Policy Roles"; illustrative amounts, not current prices or product offers. No assumption of salary, bank ownership or spare income.

es-MX.scenario: Ejemplos ficticios en pesos mexicanos para "Lee quién y qué está cubierto"; montos ilustrativos, no precios vigentes ni ofertas. No se supone nómina, cuenta bancaria ni dinero sobrante.

pt-BR.scenario: Exemplos fictícios em reais para "Leia quem e o que está coberto"; valores ilustrativos, não preços atuais nem ofertas. Sem supor salário, conta bancária ou dinheiro sobrando.

objective.observable_action: Identify the policyholder, insured event and beneficiary in a fictional policy.
objective.success_criterion: Complete the fresh-context transfer using only its visible information.

instruction.relevance: A policy identifies the contracting person, the covered event and who receives a benefit; these roles need not be identical.
instruction.misconception: The person paying always receives the benefit, and a named person means every event is covered.
instruction.numeracy_support: Use only the visible fictional amounts and conditions; earlier arithmetic is preparation, not a hidden financial assumption.

evidence.reasoning: Read who holds the contract, which event triggers coverage, and who receives the benefit. Do not infer roles from names.
Ana is explicitly named as the contracting policyholder.
The stated insured event must match the policy wording.
The named beneficiary receives the benefit under the stated terms.
The missing event terms prevent deciding what triggers coverage.
The contract can assign multiple roles to the same person.
Pat is the beneficiary identified in the stated contract.

delayed_retrieval.fresh_context: Retrieve this competence in the declared later course reviews and through the existing shared review system.
